item.title: Magnetic flux ring splitting near a Navier-Stokes singularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.22510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: OpenAI reports a forced Navier-Stokes flow that becomes singular in finite time, raising the question of its physical consequences. Magnetic reconnection offers a test through the splitting and merging of flux structures. We use resistive magnetohydrodynamics to simulate a magnetic ring driven by an imposed, regularized flow that reproduces the geometry and scaling of the collapsing core. At the nominal singular time, we remove the imposed drive and allow the system to evolve freely. Reconnections before and after release split the ring into two or more daughter rings through bifurcations of the poloidal flux function, with Lorentz feedback selecting the bifurcation type. Unequal winding by the swirl above and below the midplane produces asymmetric toroidal magnetic stresses, unfolding the kinematic pitchfork-like transition into a fold. For single-island splits, the cusp normal form predicts the asymmetry of the daughter rings without adjustable parameters. Three-dimensional simulations retain the splits and merger, confirming that approach to hydrodynamic blow-up can trigger magnetic restructuring.
item.dc:creator: Antti J. Niemi

item.title: Stability and Nonlinear Dynamics of Field-Driven Extended Domain Walls with Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction
item.description: arXiv:2610.23413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the stability and non-linear dynamics of extended domain walls (DWs) with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) driven by an external magnetic field in the clean limit (i.e., in the absence of disorder and thermal fluctuations). We show that for moderate DMI strengths, the dynamics in both the low- and high-field regimes are accurately described by a rigid-wall Walker model that neglects flexural degrees of freedom. At intermediate fields, however, the system undergoes a transition into a non-trivial spatio-temporally chaotic regime characterized by dynamically roughened domain walls displaying single- or multi-valued profiles. The phase boundaries delimiting this regime in the magnetic field-DMI phase space are computed using a linear stability analysis based on Floquet theory applied to the extended domain wall, explicitly accounting for DMI and internal phase dynamics. Our theoretical analysis and predicted phase diagram are fully supported by numerical micromagnetic simulations solving the full Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.
item.dc:creator: Enzo Fabrizio Pusiol, Alberto Rosso, Alejandro B. Kolton

item.title: Topological Magnetism in 2D and 3D: Skyrmions and Hopfions. Classical and quantum approaches
item.description: arXiv:2610.23490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss the properties of ferromagnetic skyrmions in relation to the Dzyaloshinskii Moriya interaction, nonlinear sigma models, merons, vortices, frustration, and dipole dipole interactions. Particular attention is given to skyrmion skyrmion interactions and to the dynamical equations governing magnetic textures, including the Landau Lifshitz Gilbert, Thiele, and Landau Lifshitz Bloch equations. The review subsequently extends the discussion to antiferromagnetic systems and to topological structures in three dimensions, with emphasis on Hopfions and their topological characterization. We then examine quantum skyrmions, including approaches that go beyond the semiclassical description, and discuss the emergence of quantum Hopfions. The theoretical framework is complemented by appendices presenting analytical solutions and ansatzes for skyrmions, spin coherent states and path integrals, quantum antiferromagnets, spin torques, fiber-bundle concepts and the Hopf map, and the Euler Lagrange formalism in three dimensions. By connecting continuum field theory, magnetic dynamics, topology, and quantum mechanics, this review aims to provide a coherent framework for understanding the formation, stability, dynamics, interactions, and quantum properties of topological magnetic textures across different dimensions and magnetic systems.
item.dc:creator: ANtonio S T Pires

item.title: Crystal Field-Phonon Coupling in ErFeO$_3$ Single Crystal Via Inelastic Neutron Scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.23015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Crystal-field (CF) excitations and their coupling to lattice vibrations were investigated in ErFeO$_3$ using inelastic neutron scattering. Pronounced modifications of the excitation spectra, including energy shifts, intensity redistribution, and linewidth changes, were observed as a consequence of CF-phonon coupling. Significant renormalization of the first and second CF excitations, located near 5 meV and 12 meV, respectively, was detected along both transverse and longitudinal directions in the vicinity of the reciprocal-space point Q = (2, 0, 4). The coupling effects become more prominent as the temperature increases from 300 K to 650 K, while a slight suppression is observed at 750 K. Remarkably, CF excitation peaks that are strongly weakened by thermal population effects re-emerge in specific momentum regions through interaction with phonon modes. The coupled excitations exhibit characteristic signatures of hybridization, including energy renormalization, intensity enhancement, and linewidth narrowing. Density-functional-theory-based phonon calculations further support the interpretation of CF-phonon coupling in ErFeO3. These results demonstrate that strong interactions between CF excitations and lattice vibrations can substantially modify the excitation spectra in rare-earth orthoferrites.
item.dc:creator: Guochu Deng, Xiaoxuan Ma, Wanting Yang, Wei Ren, Shixun Cao, Zhenxiang Cheng, Garry J. McIntyre

item.title: Electron--phonon matrix elements from eigenvalue projection within the projector augmented-wave method
item.description: arXiv:2503.11013v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a finite-displacement approach to electron--phonon matrix elements that requires only eigenvalues and wave functions from the displaced calculations, for both norm-conserving pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave (PAW) method. Extending the eigenvalue-projectability approach, previously formulated for norm-conserving pseudopotentials, we reconstruct the displaced Hamiltonian from the displaced eigenvalues and from overlaps evaluated in the PAW metric of each displaced structure. Analytic terms constructed from the PAW dataset then yield the all-electron matrix element, without derivatives of the local potential or of the PAW strengths. The approach therefore applies in principle to any electronic-structure method available in PAW. To reduce the supercell cost, we combine it with nondiagonal supercells that sample the Brillouin zone equivalently to the primitive cell and recover the full matrix elements by crystal symmetry. Implemented in the ARES-EPC code, the method reproduces matrix elements from density-functional perturbation theory and from VASP+phelel for seven materials with mean absolute errors below 0.5 meV. Nondiagonal supercells reproduce the diagonal-supercell results to the same accuracy and reduce the cost of the displaced calculations by up to a factor of 23.
item.dc:creator: Qian Wang, Yu Xie, Yanming Ma

item.title: Higher-Dimensional Information Lattice: Quantum State Characterization through Inclusion-Exclusion Local Information
item.description: arXiv:2512.20793v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Developing a local description of quantum information is a central problem in quantum many-body physics: the goal is to identify how correlations are organized across positions and scales without choosing specific observables. We introduce a higher-dimensional information lattice, an inclusion-exclusion construction that decomposes the von Neumann information of reduced density matrices into contributions labeled by subsystem position and scale. Above one dimension, overlapping subsystems can form loops, allowing information associated with one subsystem to be inferred nonlocally from the density matrices of others. The sign of the inclusion-exclusion information resolves such overlap redundancies in position and scale: positive values mark positions and scales with net information gain, while negative values occur where redundant contributions dominate new ones. We implement the construction in two dimensions and apply it to many-body ground states with distinct entanglement structures. For localized states, such as disordered-localized states or gapped ground states of local Hamiltonians, the local information decays exponentially along different directions, defining direction-dependent information length scales. In critical states with a Fermi surface, decay becomes algebraic, with dominant directions tied to the velocity of gapless modes. In the toric code, topological order manifests as a negative information value at the largest lattice scale, interpreted as global information redundancy between the smallest loop-enclosing overlapping subsystems. We also isolate the universal information carried by edge states and locate the signatures of non-Abelian fusion channels in position and scale. Our results establish the higher-dimensional information lattice as a framework for resolving universal correlation structures through the spatial and scale distribution of quantum information.
item.dc:creator: Ian Matthias Fl\'or, Claudia Artiaco, Thomas Klein Kvorning, Jens H. Bardarson

item.title: Geometric heat pumping on a quantum processor
item.description: arXiv:2610.09062v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Geometric heat pumping is the transfer of energy between reservoirs at equal temperature where the heat exchanged in an adiabatic cycle depends only on the driving contour in parameter space. We implement this mechanism on a superconducting quantum processor using a collision model, where a driven qubit interacts repeatedly with two ancilla qubits that are prepared in thermal states and emulate the reservoirs. Energy measurements before and after each interaction provide a calorimetric record of the heat exchanged with each reservoir. By reversing the driving contour, we extract a heat contribution associated with pumping. Its dependence on the period and on the contour follows exact simulations of the collision model, without adjustable parameters, and approaches in the slow-driving regime the geometric limit of the corresponding Lindblad dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Ger\'onimo J. Caselli, Luis O. Manuel, Liliana Arrachea, Pablo S. Cornaglia

item.title: Compact Fully Integrated Alignment-Free and Linearly Polarized Ho$^{3+}$ Single-Frequency Waveguide Laser
item.description: arXiv:2610.09435v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report, for the first time, a fully integrated Ho$^{3+}$-doped fluoride glass waveguide laser incorporating a femtosecond laser-inscribed waveguide and waveguide Bragg grating. A line-by-line inscription technique was employed to fabricate the Bragg gratings, yielding highly consistent and reproducible grating characteristics with precise control of the Bragg resonance wavelength. A compact 12.4 mm cavity achieves stable single-frequency lasing at 2062.21 nm with a linewidth of less than 5 MHz. The laser exhibits intrinsically linearly polarized emission. This alignment-free architecture provides a compact and robust platform for integrated mid-infrared single-frequency laser sources.
item.dc:creator: Jeswin Jacob, T Toney Fernandez, Dale Otten, Ori Henderson-Sapir, Karen Privat, David Lancaster
